stop_condition: Every round-5 finding is verified resolved BY MEASUREMENT or re-filed with fresh evidence, no round-5 repair introduced a new defect of its own, and no critical/high finding remains in the PATH_NO_TIMEOUT allowlist, the timed_out inference text, or the QA_TRACKING_DIR guards.

findings.evidence: MEASURED WITH A MUTANT, NOT ARGUED. 10.3 asserts `pgrep -f "sleep 20; echo should-not-finish"` finds nothing and claims in its own assertion name that this proves 'tree-kill actually worked, not just reported'. The process that actually leaks is the bare `sleep 20` GRANDCHILD, whose command line is the two words `sleep 20` and does NOT contain the pattern. Mutant = a COPY of qa-gate.sh with the process-GROUP kills at :13450 and :13462 replaced by `:` (mutation confirmed by short-token read-back: 2 hits of `MUTATED: group`, 0 hits of the original `kill -TERM -- "-$child_pid"`; `bash -n` rc=0). Three cases, one fixture, probe-d-leakcheck.sh. (a) SHIPPED script, full allowdir: 10.3's instrument 0, direct process listing 0 -- no leak, correct. (b) group-kill removed AND `ps` absent from the allowdir (the mechanical model of 'the tree-kill regressed to a single-process kill'): 10.3's instrument returns 0 AND THE ASSERTION PASSES, while a direct `ps -axo pid,ppid,command` shows a real orphan, `12982 1 sleep 20`, reparented to init. (c) group-kill removed but `ps` present: no leak -- the ps tree-walk alone suffices, which is why (b) needs both disabled. Separately measured, the live-process direction: `pgrep -f 'sleep 20; echo should-not-finish'` returns 1 against an IN-FLIGHT wrapper and 0 the moment only the wrapper is killed, with the orphan still alive. So 10.3 sees the wrapper and is blind to the leaf. THIS IS THE SHAPE THE SAME FILE WARNS ABOUT 60 LINES ABOVE, at :489-495: 'a non-vacuity check that the failure mode satisfies is not a non-vacuity check ... do not treat 10.0 alone as sufficient ever again.'
findings.description: SEVERITY MEDIUM, NOT HIGH, AND THE REASONING IS RECORDED SO A LATER READER SEES IT RATHER THAN THE VERDICT. Not HIGH because, unlike R5-F2, NOTHING IS BROKEN ON ANY HOST: the shipped code is correct, no leak occurs, and the failure requires a future regression in TWO redundant mechanisms (the ps tree-walk AND the process-group kill). 10.3 still catches a DIFFERENT real failure mode -- watchdog never fires, wrapper still alive, pgrep matches (measured: 1 hit). The harm is a latent coverage gap plus a false claim in an assertion name, which matches this arc's own MEDIUM precedent (R5-F3, R5-F4), not its HIGH one. The 'fifth consecutive round of this class IS the severity' reasoning that lifted R5-F1 to HIGH does NOT transfer: this is a first examination of this leg, not a fifth failed repair of it. NOTE THE LEG IS OLDER THAN THE LOOP -- 10.3 has been in this file since round 2, and QA read it in round 5 and called it 'otherwise sound'. BINDING REPAIR, PRE-VERIFIED BEFORE PRESCRIBING (probe-h-repair.sh; round 4's R4-F4 instruction was under-specified against QA's own evidence and that mistake is deliberately not repeated): move the uniqueness into the sleep DURATION and grep for that. With `sleep 2011` in place of `sleep 20`, pattern `pgrep -f 'sleep 2011'` -> 2 hits against a live wrapper (wrapper + leaf), 1 hit against the orphan after the wrapper is killed (the current pattern gets 0 there), and 0 hits with an unrelated `sleep 20` running, so it gains sight without gaining false positives. ONE EDIT FIXES A SECOND THING: R5-F5 closed the 13.A-to-10.3 collision, but 10.1's OWN string is still shared between two CONCURRENT runs of this spec, and the operative vector is measured to be the live wrapper (1 pgrep hit during its ~2s window), so instance A's in-flight 10.1 can still trip instance B's 10.3. Apply a distinct duration to 10.1/10.3 and to 13.A together.

findings.evidence: THE COMMENT STATES A MECHANISM THAT IS MEASURABLY NOT THE OPERATIVE ONE. It justifies the rename by 'a leaked 13.A ORPHAN from one concurrent run of this spec falsely tripping 10.3 in ANOTHER concurrent run'. Measured (R6-F1's evidence block): the orphan is a bare `sleep 20` and is INVISIBLE to `pgrep -f` on the full command string -- 0 hits. The real vector is the LIVE `bash -c "sleep 20; echo ..."` wrapper during 13.A's own 3-second window, which pgrep -f DOES match at 1 hit. The rename is correct and sufficient for the real vector; only the stated cause is wrong.
findings.description: THIS ERROR IS QA'S OWN, NOT THE IMPLEMENTER'S, AND IS FILED AGAINST QA'S OWN ROUND-5 EVIDENCE. The orphan mechanism was asserted in R5-F5's evidence block; the implementer implemented the prescribed repair faithfully and repeated the mechanism QA supplied. It is filed at all only because this arc has already established (R5-F4) that an inverted causal story in a comment is itself a finding, and consistency requires QA apply that standard to text it authored. BINDING REPAIR: one sentence, folded into R6-F1's edit -- name the live in-flight wrapper as the vector, and note that the orphan is invisible to this instrument (which is R6-F1).

findings.location: the implementer's durable COMPLETION record for fix round 4 (the disclosure paragraph); the code it describes is .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh:227 versus :87-154
findings.evidence: The disclosure states that this fixture's override file 'currently short-circuits (npm/pytest/go/cargo probing)'. It does not. `grep -n 'read_override' .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh` puts the override application at :227, AFTER the manifest chain at :87-154: the chain RUNS and simply does not match, because the fixture has no manifest files. Those branches also never INVOKE npm/go/cargo -- they only assemble command strings -- and their branch-local `command -v ruff|flake8|pylint|mypy|pyright` calls do not require the binary to be present. detect-stack.sh's ONLY unconditional external invocations are `head`, `tr` and `sed` (read_override, :79), all three of which ARE on NO_TIMEOUT_TOOLS and all three of which fail LOUDLY when removed (R6-F4's table).
findings.description: MECHANISM WRONG, CONSEQUENCE RIGHT, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS -- the disclosure's actual claim, that an omitted tool would surface as a NEW 'command not found' under PATH_NO_TIMEOUT specifically rather than as a 10.0b failure, is correct and is exactly the right thing to have disclosed. Filed at LOW because it lives in the durable audit trail, where a later reader chasing this residual would look in the wrong place. BINDING REPAIR: correct the sentence when follow-up (b) is filed.

findings.location: RECORD, NOT A DEFECT -- the ruling on the implementer's self-applied critique, and the general rule it yields
findings.evidence: THE GENERAL RULE, STATED SO IT OUTLIVES THIS FIX: WHAT SEPARATES A DANGEROUS GUARD FROM A MERELY IMPERFECT ONE IS NOT 'DOES IT FAIL LOUDLY' BUT 'IS ITS FAILURE HOST-DEPENDENT'. A defect that is invisible on the authoring host and fatal elsewhere cannot be found by running the suite, however many times it is run; a defect that fails identically on every host is tested every time anyone runs it anywhere. The denylist had the first property -- it was a BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op on this authoring box (which has neither timeout nor gtimeout) and removed the entire toolchain on ubuntu-latest -- so 88/88 here was never evidence about it. The allowlist has the second: it resolves each named tool wherever it lives and symlinks it into one directory, so its only failure mode (an incomplete list) fails the same way everywhere, and THIS BOX'S OWN RUN IS A VALID TEST OF IT. That is what converts 119/119 on this host from weak evidence into adequate evidence, and it is the reason round 6 can approve where round 5 could not. THE PROOF, NOT THE ARGUMENT (probe-c-omission.sh: delete one tool at a time from the built allowdir, run Section 10.1's exact invocation shape, nine tools): LOUD, i.e. an immediately failing named assertion -- date rc=127, tr rc=127, mkdir rc=2, jq rc=2, sed result=none, head result=none. SILENT -- ps, rm, cat. The three silent ones are silent BECAUSE THEY DID NOT MATTER: ps is covered by the process-GROUP kill at qa-gate.sh:13450/:13462, demonstrated by removing that kill and watching a real orphan appear (R6-F1 case b) and not appear with ps restored (case c); rm and cat are not on the exercised path. Six of nine loud at a named assertion, three silent and provably inconsequential. AND 10.0b DEMONSTRATED ITSELF UNPROMPTED, which is worth more than any constructed mutation: the first synthetic GNU layout QA built genuinely lacked `bd` (it lives in ~/.local/bin, not in a /usr/bin-shaped tree), and the control fired on its own the first time it was handed a real missing tool -- NO_TIMEOUT_SELFCHECK_MISSING=' bd'. No coaxing, no seeded fault.
findings.description: RULING: the allowlist's negative control does NOT inherit the denylist's flaw. 10.0b fires whenever a tool ON THE LIST fails to resolve under PATH_NO_TIMEOUT -- covering not-installed, resolution failure, ln failure, and the whole 'the filter removed something on the list' class, which is precisely the class the denylist failed. It does not cover 'needed but not on the list', and that is a RECORDED RESIDUAL rather than a block, bounded by the table above and already disclosed honestly by the implementer, which QA credits as the most valuable paragraph of the fix round. FIX VERIFICATION FOR R5-F2, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: synthetic GNU layout rebuilt from scratch (1530 co-located entries plus a WORKING timeout -- verified faithful: 124 over `sleep 5` at 1s, 7 over `exit 7`, and 124 passed through from a self-inflicted `exit 124`). Old denylist (reconstructed -- the pre-fix text is unrecoverable because green-check.test.sh is untracked, and it is labelled a reconstruction) on that layout: output PATH empty, Section 10.1 invocation rc=127, no JSON. New allowlist (extracted VERBATIM, `awk 'NR>=247 && NR<=286'`) on the SAME layout: 22 tools preserved, timeout and gtimeout both unresolvable, 10.0b empty, and Section 10.1's exact invocation shape returns rc=0 result=red exit_code=124 dispatch=watchdog timed_out=true -- every 10.1/10.1b assertion passing on the host class that produced rc=127 last round. The fix SURVIVES the layout that broke its predecessor; it does not merely differ from it.

findings.location: RECORD, NOT A DEFECT -- convergence assessment and the limitations of this review
findings.evidence: CONVERGENCE, AS A FALSIFIABLE CLAIM ABOUT THE LOOP'S DYNAMICS RATHER THAN A FEELING ABOUT DIMINISHING RETURNS. Rounds 3, 4 and 5 each found defects INTRODUCED BY THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S OWN REPAIR: R4-F1's overclaim came from round 3's fix, R5-F2's denylist came from round 4's fix, and R5-F1's STRONGER false clause came from round 4's fix. That is the signature of a non-converging loop -- each repair generating its own defect. This round QA checked all six repairs specifically for that property and NONE of them had it: the allowlist survives the GNU layout end to end and its new control demonstrably fires; the writability probe closes its case without breaking the case already closed (5 pathological states, no gap); the timed_out text is true on all five surfaces with the only surviving instance of the false clause being an explicitly quoted retraction at qa-gate.sh:13238; the 120 figure reproduces from its own cited command; the rename is textually effective; the credit is correct and 13.C-STATIC is verified non-vacuous. AND THE ONE MEDIUM IS OLDER THAN THE LOOP -- 10.3 has been in this file since round 2 and QA read it in round 5 and called it sound -- which distinguishes 'reaching a lower stratum' from 'new damage'. NON-VACUITY, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 10.0b fired on a genuinely missing bd; 14.1b reports rc=0 result=red against the pre-R5-F3 code, i.e. the phantom red itself, so reverting the fix turns it red; 13.C-STATIC's old pattern reads 0 in the shipped file but DOES match a reconstructed pre-R4-F3 line, and its new pattern reads exactly 2 (the timeout and gtimeout branches at :13396 and :13409).
findings.description: LIMITATIONS OF THIS REVIEW, RECORDED SO THE EVIDENCE IS NOT READ AS STRONGER THAN IT IS. (1) NO REAL GNU/LINUX RUN. QA got closer than round 5 -- the allowlist is BUILT from a GNU layout and Section 10.1 runs green under it -- but could not run the WHOLE spec under a simulated GNU PATH because `bd init` HANGS under it. Discriminating control: `bd init` completes rc=0 under the ambient PATH in the same conditions and is still running at 20s under the synthetic one, so the hang is QA'S HARNESS, not the change; it was killed immediately to honour the store-quiet constraint. The residual gap is narrow, because Sections 10/11's host-sensitivity is entirely PATH_NO_TIMEOUT's CONTENTS, which were verified directly. One real Linux run now costs one CI trigger rather than a review round. (2) CODE-GRAPH IS DEGRADED, OPERATOR-VISIBLE: `impact_of` and `symbol_callers` both fail with 'index DB is corrupt at .claude/.code-graph/index.db' / 'memory access out of bounds'. The index was deliberately NOT rebuilt mid-review under load. The MECHANICAL per-file impact report is present and populated (server=code-graph, 39 files, qa-gate.sh at 1462 callers within depth 5, 0 file-level dependents), so that half of 3a stands; the SYMBOL-level pass was done by hand, and the consumer set is exactly qa-gate.sh, green-check.test.sh, design-accessors.test.sh, design-conform.test.sh, run-tests.sh, review-check.sh, the three specialist prompts, docs/AGENTS.md and qa.md, none of which restates timed_out semantics. This is a FRESH instance of the corruption class tracked under the closed task dxz and is worth an operator's attention. (3) THE OLD DENYLIST SOURCE IS UNRECOVERABLE (green-check.test.sh is untracked), so the contrast run used a labelled RECONSTRUCTION of the shape the round-5 record describes, not verbatim pre-fix source. (4) QA'S OWN ERROR THIS ROUND, CORRECTED BEFORE IT REACHED THIS ARTIFACT: the round-6 report initially stated reviewer_pin as 'claude-fable-5', taken from prose inside QA's own instructions rather than from the file. `sed -n '1,12p' .claude/agents/qa.md` reads `model: claude-opus-5`, which is what this artifact carries. Same class as the numbers this arc keeps filing -- an identifier taken from prose instead of from the artifact that defines it.
